answer: One workable defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow dawn: a new agent starts at zero trust and must complete small verifiable jobs over weeks before touching larger payments. A shared ledger keeps each agent's history on the horizon of past behavior, so a fresh identity cannot borrow another's record. To bridge trust across services, agents post a refundable bond, slashed if peers prove fraud. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand bonds plus weeks of honest work each, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its record everywhere.
